proof.criterion: A7 (R6), the round's first fix - every Dispatch view that reads the agent list shows a refilling state while the listener refills, on every server process and not only the one whose call met the refusal (dispatch://INFRA-261 spec v14, third acceptance line)
proof.surface: two real `envoy-dispatch` processes on one database, one real Envoy listener and one real nats-server, all built from this head; the issue read's route status and GET /api/v1/agents on each process
proof.observed: With NATS stopped until the listener answered `503 {"code":"refilling"}`, every read on both processes, in both directions, answered the refill: process A (which fetched) `{"route_status":"unknown","route_status_reason":"refilling"}` and `503 ENVOY_REFILLING [Retry-After: 5]`; process B, reading the row A stored, the same; then after B's own fetch stored its silence, A again the same. Last round the same rig at 404283b6720c had B read `unreachable` and answer `503 ENVOY_UNAVAILABLE`, and A flip to `unreachable` after B's fetch. `PASS a refill one server met is a refill on every server, route status and the Agents list`.
proof.negativeControl: The same rig then killed the listener outright, so the silence is a listener that is gone rather than one refilling: both processes read `{"route_status":"unknown","route_status_reason":"unreachable"}` and answered `503 ENVOY_UNAVAILABLE`, with no refilling reason left over from the answer before it - `PASS a listener that is gone reads unreachable on both servers`. A fix that made every silence read as a refill would fail that half.

proof.criterion: A7 (R6) - the stored reason must not outlive the answer it came from, including beside the release before this one, which writes the row naming neither the reason nor its sent_at
proof.surface: the real route_roster table of a database an `envoy-dispatch` of this head migrated, exercised with the two upsert shapes themselves (the release's own storeRouteRosterQuery, then the previous release's, which names only answered, sessions, sent_at and expires_at)
proof.command: psql against a scratch database the head's envoy-dispatch had migrated: insert the new release's refilling silence, read `case when reason_sent_at = sent_at then reason end`, then apply the previous release's upsert at a later sent_at and read it again
proof.observed: The schema carries `reason`, `retry_after` and `reason_sent_at` beside the old columns. After the new release's write the read gives `reason=refilling`; after the previous release's write at a later sent_at the read gives `reason=` (empty) while the stored column still literally holds `refilling`, so the guard, and not the column, decides. An empty reason is `model.RouteReasonUnreachable` in `remember`, which is how that release answers its own silence.
proof.negativeControl: The first read is the control for the second: the same row, the same query, reads `refilling` while reason_sent_at is its own sent_at and nothing while it is not, so the empty answer is the guard's doing and not a column that was never written.

proof.criterion: A6, the round's second fix - a refusal for a session this listener cannot name a last registration for says so, and one for a session it can still name names the time instead
proof.surface: the real listener's POST /v1/messages/send, across a stop and start of that listener
proof.observed: On the listener that watched the session reach the gone horizon: `404 {"error":"no live session ses_gone_4807","state":"gone","last_seen":1793586581076}`. After that listener was restarted, the same send: `404 {"error":"no live session ses_gone_4807; this listener does not know when it last registered","state":"gone"}`. A send to an id that never registered anywhere reads the same way. The `no live session <id>` prefix Dispatch classifies a delivery failure on (`strings.HasPrefix(resolveError, "no live session ")`, internal/dispatch/api/comment_delivery.go:59, and envoy_resolve.go:222) is kept ahead of the new clause; no caller in the tree compares the whole text.
proof.negativeControl: The first of the three sends is the control: a listener that can name the time answers `last_seen` and says nothing about not knowing, so the words are the unknown case's alone and not every refusal's.
